title: Weekly Rest & Compensation
whatItIs: Start a weekly rest after no more than six 24-hour periods. Regular: at least 45 hours. Reduced: at least 24 hours, made up in one block by the end of the third week after.

keyFacts.text: A weekly rest MUST start no later than the end of six 24-hour periods after your last weekly rest.

keyFacts: Regular weekly rest: at least 45 continuous hours. Reduced: at least 24 but under 45 hours.

keyFacts.text: In any 2 consecutive fixed weeks you MUST take 2 regular weekly rests, or 1 regular and 1 reduced.
A reduction MUST be made up in one block before the end of the third week after the week in question.

keyFacts: The make-up rest is added to another rest of at least 9 hours.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT take a regular weekly rest in the vehicle. Your employer pays for suitable accommodation.

a.label: Regular weekly rest
points: Not in the vehicle: suitable accommodation, paid by the employer

b.label: Reduced weekly rest
points: Can be in a stationary vehicle with suitable sleeping facilities

onTheTest.question: You took a reduced weekly rest of 33 hours. How many hours of rest must you make up?
onTheTest.why: 45 − 33 = 12 hours, made up in one block with a rest of at least 9 hours, by the end of the third week after.

onTheTest.question: What is the most time allowed between two weekly rests?
onTheTest.why: A weekly rest must start no later than the end of six 24-hour periods after the last one.

traps: The make-up rest must be one block: it can't be split into smaller pieces.
Your working week doesn't have to match the fixed week: it starts when your weekly rest ends.
A weekly rest that spans two weeks counts in either week, but not both.
